findings.body: The diff touches only the anyio entry in the root uv.lock: version, sdist URL/hash/size/upload-time, and the single wheel URL/hash/size/upload-time. No pyproject.toml, source, or workflow files change. The governance contract validator classifies it as L2 with one path (uv.lock), which matches the diff.
findings.title: Change is confined to a single anyio package block in uv.lock

findings.body: The dependency list is identical before and after: idna, and typing-extensions with marker python_full_version < '3.13'. The bump adds no new transitive packages and drops none. The lock resolves to the same 276 packages, and uv lock --check --offline passes.
findings.title: Dependency set and markers are unchanged

findings.body: The auditor saw only the diff and the reported check output. uv lock --check --offline confirms the lockfile is consistent with project metadata but does not prove that the new sha256 values match the files PyPI serves. The new sdist and wheel URLs follow the normal files.pythonhosted.org layout, and the upload timestamps (2026-07-12) are consistent with each other. uv sync re-verifies these hashes at install time, so a mismatch would fail loudly rather than silently. No anomaly was observed, but registry-side verification was not performed in this audit.
findings.title: Artifact hashes not independently verified against the PyPI registry

findings.body: The supplied deterministic checks cover lock consistency, whitespace, the change contract, and import anyio. None of them exercises downstream consumers of anyio (for example async HTTP or MCP/ASGI stacks) under 4.14.2. A minor release can change cancellation, task-group, or exception-group behavior in ways an import check cannot detect. The risk is mitigated by anyio's backward-compatibility policy within 4.x and by the repository's normal test suite, which this audit did not run or review.
findings.title: Minor-version bump (4.13 -> 4.14) validated only by import smoke test

findings.body: Recent history shows a separate bump (#1364) of anyio to 4.14.2 in docker/mcp-servers-source/pal/pal-mcp-server. Those environments are locked and deployed independently of the root lock. Until both PRs land, the two locks may pin different anyio versions. This is not a defect in PR #1363 and has no effect on the root environment.
findings.title: Possible transient version skew with the nested pal-mcp-server lock

remaining_risks: New sdist/wheel sha256 values were not cross-checked against PyPI by the auditor; integrity relies on uv's install-time hash verification.
Runtime compatibility of anyio 4.14.2 with downstream packages was not exercised beyond import anyio; the full test suite result was not provided.
Transient version skew between the root uv.lock and the nested pal-mcp-server lock until #1364 and #1363 are both merged.
